narrative: Material PL1__M3813B21 exhibits lumpy demand (CV=0.54) with a mean of 277.6 units/day over 130 working days; 10.8% of days recorded zero demand. Lead times average 4.1 days with moderate variability (CV=0.37) after removing two extreme data-entry errors (9,201 and 9,327 days). An (r,Q) continuous-review policy is recommended: a reorder point of 1,987 units triggers a fixed replenishment of 2,013 units, capped at the storage limit of 2,869 units. This consolidates 826 annual orders under the current MOQ-only policy into just 34, cutting total annual inventory costs by 90.6%.

research_insights.selection_rationale: The material has moderate-to-high daily demand (277.6 units/day) and relatively stable lead times (CV=0.37), making a continuous-review (r,Q) policy appropriate. EOQ minimises the sum of ordering and holding costs; the reorder point provides a statistical safety buffer calibrated to the 95th percentile of lead-time demand.
research_insights.boundary_risk: Storage capacity is fully consumed (2,869/2,869 units = safety_stock + order_quantity). Any upward revision of safety stock — e.g. due to increased demand variability or a higher service level target — would require either a capacity expansion or a reduction in order quantity, increasing order frequency and cost.
research_insights.escalation_flag: none — MOQ (84) + safety_stock (856) = 940, which is well below max_storage_units (2869). No MOQ-capacity infeasibility.
